A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyLaR and DePO. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplements support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HyLaR benchmark evaluations, RL and hyperparameter ablations, normalization experiments, and inference examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds inference-efficiency measurements, 3B-model evaluations, and attention visualizations.

M1.justification: The SFT/DePO pipeline, latent recursion, canvas compression, losses, and decoupled clipping are retained. Deterministic mode-referenced optimization and the practical unnormalized surrogate already appear in v1's supplement; they are not new method components.

E1.justification: Training datasets and the eight benchmark settings remain unchanged. The 3B evaluation uses existing benchmarks, while the new attention examples concern object attributes and spatial relationships already represented in v1.

E2.justification: Existing benchmark and RL-ablation comparator sets are retained. New Tables 3–4 add explicit efficiency comparisons with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and multi-turn DeepEyes, and smaller-scale comparisons with Qwen2.5-VL-3B and LVR-3B, reusing existing baseline families.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 3B model configuration and an H20 inference-efficiency evaluation reporting latency and memory relative to Qwen2.5-VL-7B, with 16 latent tokens for HyLaR. Previously stated training and evaluation settings are unchanged; the additions do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds bounded analyses of inference cost and smaller-model scalability. Supplementary Section 4 and Fig. S7 add two attention-localization cases. Existing latent-step, RL-algorithm, clipping, distribution, and normalization ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures for benchmark performance. The new tables retain point-estimate reporting, and the existing reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores, ablation values, and plotted results are unchanged. New Table 3 reports HyLaR latency/memory of 0.96×/0.98× versus DeepEyes' 2.28×/3.64×, normalized to Qwen2.5-VL-7B. Table 4 adds 3B scores: HyLaR improves over its backbone on five of six benchmarks but scores lower on V*, 68.58 versus 70.68. Fig. S7 adds qualitative attention results.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and supplementary derivations are unchanged. Both versions contain the mode-referenced ratio, closed-form vMF KL derivation, and qualification that the implemented unnormalized surrogate loses the exact probabilistic interpretation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about hybrid latent reasoning, DePO, and benchmark superiority. Additional experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning efficiency, smaller-model generalization, and latent tokens functioning as semantic pointers that provide visual grounding. Its claim of consistent 3B superiority across all benchmarks conflicts with Table 4's V* result. Existing interpretations and the normalization qualification are retained.

D1.justification: The new efficiency experiment identifies H20 hardware, 16 latent tokens, a long-CoT Qwen baseline, and multi-turn DeepEyes. Its workload and timing/memory measurement procedures remain unspecified. Existing training details, data counts, software references, hyperparameter tables, and code-access statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Yu et al., The Latent Space: Foundation, Evolution, Mechanism, Ability, and Outlook, as reference 43 in v2. Existing positioning against latent-reasoning methods remains substantially unchanged; most other citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the framework overview, related-work summary, and distribution-ablation explanation, and adds short efficiency, scalability, and attention discussions. Author-affiliation formatting is updated. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two tables and the two-panel attention visualization in Fig. S7. Existing figure captions are shortened, Fig. 3 is resized and relocated, and other content shifts with pagination. v1 Tables 3–6 become v2 Tables 5–8; their contents and the six original supplementary cases are retained.

improvement.justification: The added measurements make inference cost and smaller-model applicability more assessable, while Fig. S7 provides direct visual evidence relevant to the grounding explanation. These modestly strengthen the paper without changing its original results. The gain is limited by insufficient efficiency-protocol detail and an incorrect universal 3B-superiority claim: Table 4 shows HyLaR below its backbone on V*, 68.58 versus 70.68.
